newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: 30,000 students stage renewed Serbia protest.
newsitem.headline: 30,000 students stage renewed Serbia protest.

text.p: As many as 30,000 students took to the streets of Belgrade on Tuesday, marking the 23rd day of mass protests against the Socialist rule of Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic, eyewitnesses said.
The crowd was on its way to pass by the Yugoslav federal parliament, in session for the first time since a disputed November 17 municipal election which the opposition said it won.
Serbian opposition parties boycotted the parliament's session, vowing to stay away until Milosevic acknowledged he had cheated them of their local election victory.

The pro-democracy rallies have become a daily ritual in the capital and other large cities across Serbia, posing the most sustained challenge to Milosevic's nine-year rule during which he has kept a tight grip on state institutions.
The Zajedno (Together) coalition of opposition parties was expected to stage its daily protest march later on Tuesday.

Belgrade has come under a barrage of western criticism for its handling of the elections. NATO on Tuesday "strongly deplored" the cancellation of election results and called on Milosevic to reverse the decision.
